Geography.name: Amazon River
Geography.definition: The Amazon River in South America is the world's largest river by discharge volume of water and is widely considered the second-longest river system. Flowing primarily through Peru and Brazil into the Atlantic Ocean, its vast basin supports the planet's largest tropical rainforest.
key_facts: It accounts for approximately 20% of the world's total river discharge into the oceans.
The traditionally accepted source of the Amazon River is high in the Peruvian Andes at Nevado Mismi.
There are no bridges built across the main stem of the Amazon River due to its extreme width, seasonal flooding, and dense surrounding rainforest.
